Timing/seasonality of recharge pulses relative to snowmelt-driven infiltration events
Water-table depth constraint using Fan 2013 WTD prior and nearby USGS wells

parsed.n_justification: The dominant control on infiltration-to-recharge lag is water-table depth, which spans meters (valley) to tens of meters (upland) across the 352-1977 m elevation gradient. Five columns sample the WTD/elevation/texture continuum: two shallow valley sites, one mid-slope, and two deep upland sites, enough to bracket the travel-time response without over-fitting a data-sparse basin.
assumptions: PFLOTRAN is coupled beneath ELM to solve variably-saturated 1-D vertical flow (Richards) with the water table as a Dirichlet/seepage lower boundary set from Fan 2013 WTD priors and nearest USGS well levels.
A multi-year run (1980-2018) is used so that deep-column travel times (potentially multi-year in upland sites) are captured; the first ~5-10 years are treated as spin-up.
'Today's infiltration' is diagnosed via a virtual tracer / age-tracking in the vadose zone (or via cross-correlation of QINFL and QRECHARGE lag) since ELM alone does not tag water parcels.
1980-1985 forcing is cycled for additional spin-up if hydrostatic equilibrium of the deep vadose profile is not reached by model year 5.
Column vadose-zone thickness is set per site from WTD (shallow ~2-5 m, deep ~20-40 m) with refined vertical layering near the surface and water table.
Recharge timing is reported as a model result only; magnitude is unvalidated due to absent recharge observations.
